docs.title: ollamarun
docs.text:
A terminal agent harness for Ollama — a personal project about how far local models go when you hand them tools.

ollamarun began as a nicer ollama run: streamed markdown, 2D Unicode math, sessions that actually persist. It has since grown into a full harness — an approval-gated tool loop, two front ends, remote inference, context/GPU placement fitting, and an HTTP API layer (ollamarun serve) that speaks both the OpenAI API and its own native agent API.

Every ollama run flag (ollama 0.34) is accepted and extended, so it still doubles as a drop-in replacement for the CLI it started as.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Needs Linux, Python 3.10+ and a reachable Ollama server (default 127.0.0.1:11434).

$ pip install --user rich requests prompt_toolkit
$ ./ollamarun qwen3:8b "explain this repo"    # one-shot
$ ./ollamarun qwen3:8b                        # interactive REPL

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Early, single-developer and moving. Built against one Linux box and a small Tailscale fleet; Python 3.10; a few tools are wired to my own side projects and degrade gracefully when those are absent. Rough edges are part of the deal — expect the structure to keep changing as the learning continues.

More background in Project overview; Apache-2.0 · Acknowledgements.

docs.title: API overview
docs.text:
ollamarun serve runs a local HTTP API in front of Ollama, so any OpenAI client can use the local models. The listener is LAN-accessible by default (0.0.0.0:11440); --bind IP / --port N narrow or change it and are separate from the upstream --host / --remote, which pick the Ollama machine:

$ ollamarun serve [--bind IP] [--port N] [--host HOST | --remote NAME] [--keep-loaded]

Trusted-network-only

The service has no authentication, and the bind address is its only boundary. Keep it on the LAN/tailnet and never expose the port to the public internet.

Two surfaces share the process:

  • OpenAI API — GET /v1/models, POST /v1/chat/completions and POST /v1/embeddings: model turns only, a stateless translation proxy.
  • Agent API — full agent turns with the internal tool loop, approvals, sessions, files/artifacts and context fits.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Disconnects and cancellation. A dropped event stream is an unsubscribe — the turn keeps running (its results land in the session) unless it asked for "cancel_on_disconnect": true. POST .../cancel cancels explicitly: it aborts the in-flight generation, kills cancellable subprocesses, resolves a waiting approval as cancelled and persists the terminal state.

Shutdown is an ordered lifecycle: the listener stops accepting, new turns and fits are refused (503 server_shutting_down), parked approvals resolve as cancelled, in-flight HTTP handlers drain within serve_shutdown_timeout, and serve_unload_on_exit (default true) unloads only the models this server actually used — embedding models stay resident and a parallel CLI session's models are never touched (--keep-loaded disables it).

docs.title: Compatibility testing
docs.text:
The surface is pinned by the project's test suite, which a client can trust as the compatibility contract: a required round-trip through the official openai SDK (models, embeddings in both encodings, completions with n > 1, streaming with usage, typed tool calls, the 400 mappings, a mid-stream failure) plus the deterministic request/response matrix and a real-process smoke of ollamarun serve — python3 test_ollamarun.py, with --live adding a real-backend pass (models, completions, embeddings, one agent turn).

The next pages:

  • Security and limits — the serve_* boundaries.
  • Example clients — two runnable reference clients.
  • Config file — the full serve_* key matrix.

docs.title: Example clients
docs.text:
Two reference clients under examples/ double as integration checks — both print a PASS/SKIP/FAIL line per step and exit non-zero on a failure:

  • examples/openai_client.py — the official openai SDK against the /v1 surface: the model list, a completion, streaming with usage, embeddings (the SDK's default base64 encoding), n = 2 and a tools request. Needs the SDK (pip install --user openai); pass a chat model:
$ python3 examples/openai_client.py --model qwen3:8b
  • examples/agent_client.py — the native agent flow over plain HTTP: submit a turn, follow the typed SSE stream, resolve a parked approval, read the session summary. --mode interactive --approve run exercises the approval path; --session-id continues an existing session:
$ python3 examples/agent_client.py --prompt "List the files in /tmp"

Both take --base-url for a remote or non-default listener (the OpenAI one wants the /v1 suffix).

docs.title: Security and limits
docs.text:
Trusted-network-only

The service has no authentication, and the bind address is its only boundary. Keep it on the LAN/tailnet and never expose the port to the public internet.

docs.title: Deployment and auth
docs.text: ollamarun serve is meant to run on the trusted network under the user's own service management (the serve_* keys cover the listener, limits and shutdown; the startup banner prints the surface in effect). There is deliberately no authentication yet — the bind address is the only boundary, so the port must never reach the public internet. When authentication lands it wraps these routes without reshaping them: it is a transport concern, and never a substitute for the tool-approval gate.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
The JSON body cap is serve_body_limit (default 32 MiB), and it applies to Content-Length and chunked bodies alike: a chunked upload is decoded with the cumulative decoded size checked before each chunk is read, Transfer-Encoding together with Content-Length is an ambiguity error, and malformed framing (bad sizes, missing CRLF, truncation, a missing terminal chunk, a non-chunked coding) is a structured 400.

Resolving content parts is bounded separately, because a small body can name many large inputs: serve_max_messages, serve_max_content_parts, serve_max_message_bytes, serve_max_text_bytes, serve_max_images and serve_max_image_bytes (cumulative after resolving data URIs, remote fetches and file inlines; counts fail before any fetch). Embeddings inputs are charged to the same budget (input count, per-input bytes, total text). Violations are 413 input_too_large naming the limit.

serve_request_timeout (default 30 s) is a per-operation socket timeout — a streaming response that keeps writing (heartbeats included) is never cut off by it — and serve_sse_ping_interval (default 15 s) is the SSE heartbeat.

docs.title: Model allowlist
docs.text: serve_models (default: empty) restricts which models the API exposes and accepts: names or fnmatch patterns matched against the installed models after tag normalization (qwen3 matches qwen3:latest; qwen3* matches every tag). The list applies everywhere a model is selected, listed or used — the model list, lookup, chat completions, session creation and model edits, agent turns (a stored session whose model fell out of the list is refused before it runs) and the fit endpoints — and a model outside it answers exactly like an unknown one (404 model_not_found).

docs.title: Tool workspace
docs.text: Serve runs its tool context jailed to serve_workspace (default: the directory serve started in, printed in the banner): relative paths in the file tools resolve under it, resolved escapes — symlinks included — are refused, and the run_shell/run_python working directories follow the same rule. This is an argument and default-working-directory policy, not subprocess confinement: an approved command can still reach whatever the process user can. The CLI keeps its previous behavior.

docs.title: Feature switches
docs.text:
serve_agent: false runs the process as an inference server: the native routes (turns, approvals, sessions, fits) are not registered at all (404), while models, chat completions and the /v1/files + /v1/artifacts/* endpoints keep serving — the OpenAI surface can still send file parts. One model policy applies to every route: see the allowlist above.

Every key with its default, range and zero semantics is listed in Config file.

docs.title: Approvals
docs.text:
settings.approval decides who answers a tool call:

  • "policy" (the default) applies the configured tool policy — allowlisted and rule-covered calls run, everything else is denied with a note. The serve policy is never auto; --yes remains the only CLI auto path.
  • "interactive" parks genuinely undecided calls: the turn enters waiting_approval and emits approval.required with the approval_id, the call, the reason and suggested rules.

POST /v1/agent/approvals/{id} resolves a parked decision. The first decision wins; duplicates get 409. An unanswered approval times out (config serve_approval_timeout, default 300 s) as denied: the tool result says not run: approval timed out and the model continues.

The parked event carries everything needed to decide (the client already saw it on the stream, as approval.required):

{"name": "run_shell", "args": {"command": "rm -rf build"},
 "detail": "rm -rf build", "fingerprint": "…", "reason": "catastrophic rm",
 "approval_id": "apr_…",
 "suggestions": [{"kind": "shell", "pattern": "rm -rf build",
                  "base": "", "created": "…"}]}

The decision is one POST — the body's action picks the outcome:

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/approvals/apr_… \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"action": "run"}'
{"id": "apr_…", "object": "approval", "turn_id": "trn_…", "session_id": "ses_…",
 "name": "run_shell", "status": "resolved", "action": "run", "run": true,
 "note": "confirmed", "resolved_at": "…"}
Request body Effect {"action": "run"} Run this call once {"action": "remember"} Run it, remembering the exact call for the session {"action": "rule", "rule": {"kind": "shell", "pattern": "make :*"}} Run it and store a generalized rule (call, shell, path or python) {"action": "auto"} Allow everything for the rest of this turn {"action": "deny"} Refuse it; the model gets a not-run note

The rules are the same engine the CLI uses — see Approvals and policy.

docs.title: Artifacts
Storage and retention
docs.text: Artifacts are immutable snapshots (the hash and size come from the stored bytes), live under ~/etc/data/ollamarun/artifacts/ (opaque ids, index-driven lookup, sanitized display names only, and a resolved-root containment invariant: every index/manifest path must resolve inside the store root, so a symlinked directory under it can never redirect a read or a sweep) and expire after config serve_artifact_ttl (default 7 days; the sweep also reaps stale reservations and debris at startup). The per-file cap is serve_artifact_max_bytes (default 16 MiB — the base64-in-JSON request must fit the 32 MiB body cap) and serve_artifact_quota_bytes (default 2 GiB) is reserved under a lock so concurrent uploads cannot overshoot a 507 artifact_quota_exceeded.

docs.title: Publication
docs.text: Tool outputs publish automatically (write_file/edit_file/copy_file/ move_file snapshot their result, regular files only); scripts publish explicitly through the approval-gated publish_artifact tool. Every publication emits artifact.created with the full record before tool.result, which references the ids; turn results and session metadata list the refs. A persist: false turn still registers and serves its artifacts — retention is TTL-only and shared with session-deleted conversations (deleting a session never deletes artifacts early).

docs.title: Event stream
docs.text:
GET /v1/agent/turns/{id}/events is the SSE stream for a turn. Each frame is named after its event type and carries a <turn_id>:<seq> id, so a reconnect resumes with ?after=N or Last-Event-ID:

$ curl -N 'http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/turns/trn_…/events?after=0'
id: trn_…:1
event: turn.started
data: {"id": "trn_…:1", "seq": 1, "type": "turn.started", "turn_id": "trn_…",
       "session_id": "ses_…", "ts": "…",
       "data": {"model": "qwen3:8b", "session_id": "ses_…"}}
id: trn_…:2
event: message.delta
data: {"id": "trn_…:2", "seq": 2, "type": "message.delta", "turn_id": "trn_…",
       "session_id": "ses_…", "ts": "…",
       "data": {"channel": "content", "text": "The repo is"}}
id: trn_…:3
event: tool.call
data: {"id": "trn_…:3", "seq": 3, "type": "tool.call", "turn_id": "trn_…",
       "session_id": "ses_…", "ts": "…", "data": {"name": "run_shell",
       "args": {"command": "ls -la"}, "detail": "ls -la", "round": 1}}
id: trn_…:4
event: tool.result
data: {"id": "trn_…:4", "seq": 4, "type": "tool.result", "turn_id": "trn_…",
       "session_id": "ses_…", "ts": "…", "data": {"name": "run_shell",
       "ok": true, "text": "total 42\n…", "duration": 0.03, …}}
id: trn_…:5
event: turn.completed
data: {"id": "trn_…:5", "seq": 5, "type": "turn.completed", "turn_id": "trn_…",
       "session_id": "ses_…", "ts": "…",
       "data": {"content": "…", "tool_calls": 1, "rounds": 2, "stats": {…}, …}}

docs.title: Event vocabulary
docs.text: The stream carries turn.started, message.delta, tool.call/tool.result, approval.required/approval.resolved, turn.warning and the terminal turn.completed/turn.error/turn.cancelled, each with a deterministic <turn_id>:<seq> id.

docs.title: Replay and gaps
docs.text:
A reconnecting client resumes with Last-Event-ID; a truncated buffer is reported as stream.gap, and the turn status endpoint is the recovery path afterwards. A subscription without ?after=/Last-Event-ID is live-only — nothing is replayed, so a finished turn yields an empty stream; catching-up clients pass after=0 or read the status snapshot instead.

A dropped stream is an unsubscribe, not a cancellation — see Disconnects and cancellation.

docs.title: Context fits
docs.text:
Context and placement over the API come in two speeds.

POST /v1/agent/fit estimates synchronously (no model loads) — {model?, session_id?, mode: "gpu"|"cpu", cpu_percent, gpu_layers?, apply?} — and returns the num_ctx, the bound and a report (parameters, weights, per-token KV, machine budget); apply: true writes it to the session.

# estimate only -- never loads the model; `apply` writes it to the session
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/fit \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"session_id": "ses_…", "mode": "gpu", "apply": true}'
{"object": "fit", "model": "qwen3:8b", "mode": "gpu", "num_ctx": 131072,
 "source": "estimate", "bound": "max_gpu", "gpu_layers": null, "applied": true,
 "report": {"weights_bytes": …, "kv_per_token": …, "free_bytes": …, …}}

# verify by loading: an asynchronous probe job (202), then poll it
$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/fits \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"session_id": "ses_…", "mode": "cpu", "cpu_percent": 80}'
{"id": "fit_…", "object": "fit", "status": "queued", "session_id": "ses_…",
 "mode": "cpu", "probe": true, "apply": false, "warnings": [],
 "status_url": "/v1/agent/fits/fit_…",
 "cancel_url": "/v1/agent/fits/fit_…/cancel"}

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/fits/fit_…
{"id": "fit_…", "object": "fit", "status": "completed",
 "progress": {"stage": "probe", "mode": "cpu", "ctx": 65536},
 "applied": false, "result": {"model": "qwen3:8b", "mode": "cpu",
 "num_ctx": 65536, "source": "probe", "bound": "max_cpu", …}}

POST /v1/agent/fits starts the same fit as an asynchronous probe job that verifies the boundary by actually loading the model: 202 with the job id and warnings (other resident models or active turns make it slower; prior measurements on this host make it faster), GET /v1/agent/fits/{id} for status/progress/result, POST .../cancel to stop it. A job with a session holds it — turns, edits and a second fit get 409 session_busy with active_fit_id — a global cap (serve_max_active_fits) answers 429, and completed jobs live until serve_fit_ttl.

Turn settings.num_ctx also accepts "max-gpu" / "max-cpu" (with settings.cpu_percent): the turn estimates at start — never a blocking probe — persists the fitted context and reports it as a typed session.fit event and result.fit on the turn status; a failed fit leaves the context unchanged.

serve_fit gates the whole surface: "probe" (default), "estimate" (no probing) or "off".

The CLI equivalents are in Context and placement.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
The durable record behind turns — the same JSON session store the CLI uses:

Endpoint What it does GET/POST /v1/sessions list / create sessions GET/PATCH/DELETE /v1/sessions/{id} inspect, edit (title/model/system/tags/parameters/num_ctx/gpu_layers) or trash a session; edits and deletes are refused (409 session_busy) while a turn or fit runs

A session's context size and GPU placement are first-class fields: PATCH /v1/sessions/{id} (and the turn settings) accept num_ctx (a positive integer, refused past the model's trained maximum) and gpu_layers (N, P%, +N/-N, all, cpu or auto; a change unloads the resident model, exactly like /gpu-layers).

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/sessions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model": "qwen3:8b", "title": "build log triage", "tags": ["infra"]}'
{"id": "ses_…", "object": "session", "title": "build log triage",
 "model": "qwen3:8b", "host": "http://127.0.0.1:11434", "tags": ["infra"],
 "messages": 0, "turns": 0, "system": null, "artifacts": [],
 "active_turn_id": null, "created_at": "…", "updated_at": "…"}

$ curl -s -X PATCH http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/sessions/ses_… \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"num_ctx": 32768, "gpu_layers": "80%",
         "parameters": {"temperature": 0.4}}'

Session history lives under ~/etc/data/ollamarun/sessions/ — see Storage. Context fitting over the API is on Context fits.

docs.title: Turns
docs.text:
The same ollamarun serve process also exposes ollamarun's own endpoints: instead of one inference call, a client submits a full agent turn — the internal tool loop, approvals and session persistence run server-side — and follows it over Server-Sent Events.

Endpoint What it does POST /v1/agent/turns start a full agent turn (202 + the turn id and its URLs) GET /v1/agent/turns/{id} snapshot: queued/running/waiting_approval/completed/failed/cancelled, seq, result, error (404 unknown, 410 swept) GET /v1/agent/turns/{id}/events SSE turn events (id: <turn>:<seq>, typed event: names; replay with ?after=N or Last-Event-ID) POST /v1/agent/turns/{id}/cancel request cancellation 
POST /v1/agent/turns
{
  "model": "llama3.2:3b",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Clean up /tmp/build"}],
  "persist": true,
  "settings": {
    "tools": true, "max_rounds": 8,
    "approval": "interactive",
    "system": null, "parameters": {},
    "cancel_on_disconnect": false
  }
}

For an existing session (session_id) the messages are the delta; for a new one they seed the history. Turns persist by default (persist: false runs ephemeral). settings.parameters — and the sessions' parameters field, including the PATCH merge — is validated: known Ollama options get their type and range checked (the same ranges the OpenAI mapper enforces), unknown names pass through but are bounded to scalars and small lists with size caps, and non-finite numbers or nested structures are refused with a 400.

Concrete requests — a new session seeds the history, an existing one gets the delta (persist defaults to true) — and the turn's URLs come back immediately:

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/turns \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
      "session_id": "ses_…",
      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "now file it under reports"}],
      "settings": {"approval": "interactive"}
    }'
{"id": "trn_…", "object": "turn", "session_id": "ses_…", "status": "queued",
 "created_at": "…", "status_url": "/v1/agent/turns/trn_…",
 "events_url": "/v1/agent/turns/trn_…/events",
 "cancel_url": "/v1/agent/turns/trn_…/cancel"}

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/turns \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
      "model": "qwen3:8b",
      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this repo"}],
      "persist": false,
      "settings": {"max_rounds": 4, "system": "One paragraph, no lists.",
                   "num_ctx": "max-gpu", "gpu_layers": "80%"}
    }'

The snapshot endpoint gives the same result with no stream (and a finished turn has no live events, so this — or ?after=0 — is how a late client catches up):

$ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/turns/trn_…
{"id": "trn_…", "object": "turn", "session_id": "ses_…", "status": "completed",
 "seq": 5, "result": {"status": "completed", "content": "…", "rounds": 2,
 "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 412, "completion_tokens": 96, "total_tokens": 508},
 "artifacts": [], "fit": null}, "error": null}

$ curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:11440/v1/agent/turns/trn_…/cancel
{"id": "trn_…", "object": "turn", "cancel_requested": true, "status": "running"}

docs.title: Records and limits
docs.text:
Turn records live in memory — a restart loses live turns (404/410), while session history stays under ~/etc/data/ollamarun/sessions/. One active turn per session (409 session_busy with active_turn_id; editing or deleting the session is the same 409 while the turn runs), a global cap (config serve_max_active_turns, 429), and an optional wall-clock limit per turn (config serve_turn_timeout, 0 = no limit).

  • Event stream — following a turn.
  • Approvals — resolving parked tool calls.
  • Sessions — the durable record.
  • Disconnects and cancellation.

docs.title: Chat completions
docs.text:
POST /v1/chat/completions is one model turn, streaming (stream: true) or not. Model turns are a translation proxy: one request is one /api/chat call (an n > 1 request is emulated with that many sequential generations).

from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:11440/v1", api_key="unused")
print(client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen3:8b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]).choices[0].message.content)

Supported fields: temperature, top_p, max_tokens / max_completion_tokens (→ num_predict), stop, seed, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, response_format (json_object / json_schema → Ollama format), reasoning_effort (low/medium/high → Ollama think), tools, tool_choice (auto, none, or a specific function), stream, stream_options.include_usage, and the extension system ("auto" = the built-in default prompt, text = replace it, absent = none; a client-sent system message always wins). user and metadata are accepted and ignored (tracking hints).

  • Streaming — the SSE chunk shapes.
  • Tool calls — pass-through and parallel_tool_calls.
  • n > 1 choices — emulated fan-out.
  • Vision — image_url parts.
  • Errors — strict validation and the error envelope.

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
POST /v1/embeddings maps to /api/embed: {model, input, encoding_format, dimensions, user} with input a non-empty string or array of non-empty strings (a client's token arrays are rejected explicitly), encoding_format "float" (default) or "base64" (the little-endian float32 packing the official SDK sends by default), and dimensions forwarded to the backend for models that support truncated vectors.

The response is the OpenAI list shape — {object: "list", data: [{object: "embedding", index, embedding}], model, usage: {prompt_tokens, total_tokens}} — with the token counts read from the backend.

The model must advertise the embedding capability (model_does_not_support_embeddings otherwise; an unverifiable empty capability list passes), the serve_models allowlist applies, and the resolved-input budget bounds the inputs exactly like chat content.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Request validation is strict, and every rejection is a structured error rather than a silent ignore: unknown fields anywhere (top level, tools, tool_choice, response_format wrappers), n outside 1..8 or non-integer (each emulated choice is a full generation), logprobs/top_logprobs, logit_bias, audio, non-text modalities and tool_choice: "required" are rejected with 400s; strict: true on a function tool is rejected because the backend does not enforce tool-argument schemas (strict: false is a no-op).

json_schema enforcement uses Ollama's grammar (format); only the schema object is forwarded.

Errors use the OpenAI envelope with proper status codes (400/404/405/408/413/502); upstream failures surface as stable model_not_found / backend_unreachable / backend_error messages, oversized bodies and stalled uploads are rejected before parsing, and responses never carry tracebacks or internal paths — --debug logs requests, upstream detail and tracebacks to ~/etc/logs/ollamarun.log.

Everything the backend cannot do is rejected permanently:

  • logprobs/top_logprobs — Ollama exposes no token probabilities.
  • logit_bias — no backend equivalent.
  • audio and non-text modalities — Ollama has no audio modality.
  • tool_choice: "required" — the backend cannot force a call.
  • strict: true tool schemas — tool-argument schemas are not enforced (response_format schemas are, through Ollama's format grammar).

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
Endpoint What it does GET /v1/models installed models as OpenAI model objects GET /v1/models/{id} one model (404 + error envelope when unknown)

Model selection is gated everywhere by the serve_models allowlist: a model outside it answers exactly like an unknown one (404 model_not_found).

docs.title: n > 1 choices
docs.text:
n runs that many generations (1..8, emulated sequentially, with the counters summed): each emulated choice is a full generation, so n outside 1..8 or non-integer is rejected with a 400.

Streaming responses carry per-choice indexes; the summed usage matches the non-streaming shape.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
Streaming emits OpenAI SSE only: a role chunk, content deltas, the finish chunk, an optional usage chunk (stream_options.include_usage) and data: [DONE]; thinking models surface their reasoning as the non-standard delta.reasoning_content, which normal clients ignore. A dropped streaming client cancels its own upstream generation.

The native agent surface has its own typed event stream — see Event stream.

docs.title: Tool calls
docs.text:
Client tools are passed to the backend and returned as standard tool_calls with finish_reason: "tool_calls" — they are never executed here, so this endpoint cannot trigger the agent harness. Full agent turns live under the native /v1/agent/* endpoints.

  • tool_choice accepts auto, none or a specific function; tool_choice: "required" is rejected (the backend cannot force a call).
  • parallel_tool_calls is honored: a false returns only the first tool call the backend produced (the backend cannot be told to emit a single call, so this is a truncation, not model steering).
  • strict: true on a function tool is rejected because the backend does not enforce tool-argument schemas (strict: false is a no-op). See Errors.

docs.title: Vision
docs.text:
image_url content parts accept data: URIs or http(s) URLs (fetched with explicit timeouts, at most 3 redirects and a 10 MiB cap — the SSRF caveat is the locked trusted-network boundary), are validated against the model's capabilities and refused with model_does_not_support_images when vision is absent.

A {"type": "file", "file_id": "art_…"} part resolves an uploaded artifact: text-ish files are inlined as a <file name="…"> block, images go through the same vision gate, and other binaries are described but never pretended to be processed — see Artifacts.

The CLI takes images too — --image PATH / /image PATH… | clear.

docs.title: CLI overview
docs.text:
ollamarun is the terminal harness. Every ollama run flag (ollama 0.34) is accepted and extended, so it still doubles as a drop-in replacement for the CLI it started as: run it one-shot with a prompt, or with none for the interactive REPL.

  • Agent loop, not a pipe. The model calls tools through Ollama function calling — shell, Python, files, web, your saved sessions, system stats, speech, the chemical inventory — in multi-round loops. Read-only calls run unattended; everything else asks, with numbered choices and remembered rules. See Tools.
  • Rendering that keeps up. Markdown re-renders while tokens stream, display math is laid out in 2D Unicode by a self-contained engine, thinking streams live in a collapsible panel, and a ~tok/s · ctx footer ticks with every token (--no-tps//tps switch it off). See Streaming markdown.
  • Sessions that persist. One atomic JSON per conversation plus an index under ~/etc/data/ollamarun/, with search, export (md/json/html), branch, tags and trash-put deletes. See Storage.
  • Two front ends. The prompt_toolkit inline REPL (default) or --ui tui (deprecated — see TUI): transcript pane, status bar, and an input box that stays usable while the model works.
  • Any machine on the tailnet. --remote NAME runs all inference and model management on another machine — a name defined in config remote_hosts, or any host[:port] — while sessions, files and tools stay local. See Remote inference.
  • Context and placement fitting. /num-ctx --max-gpu finds the largest window that stays fully on the GPU, /num-ctx --max-cpu N fills DRAM to N%, --probe verifies by loading and calibrates later estimates, and /gpu-layers pins layer counts. See Context and placement.
  • Model-facing text is data. Tool definitions and prompts live as JSON/Markdown under ollamarun_lib/defs/, overridable per user without touching Python. See Tool definitions and Prompts.

Start with Usage and flags, or jump straight to The REPL.

docs.title: Editor
docs.text: Two ways to bring a real editor into a conversation.

docs.title: Ctrl+G: edit the current input
docs.text:
Press Ctrl+G at the prompt and the current input opens in $OLLAMA_EDITOR — or $EDITOR when OLLAMA_EDITOR is unset, falling back to vi. The buffer is written to a temporary .md file, the editor is launched on it, and whatever you save replaces the input line when the editor exits:

$ OLLAMA_EDITOR=nano ollamarun --no-tools llama3.2:3b
llama3.2:3b › a half-written question        ← press Ctrl+G here

In the editor you fix the text, save and quit, and the prompt comes back with the new content — then Enter sends it. Tested end-to-end with a scripted editor that replaced draft text with a question: the answer that came back was for the edited prompt.

  • An editor that cannot be started prints editor failed: … and the input is left untouched.
  • OLLAMA_EDITOR is split shell-style, so OLLAMA_EDITOR="code --wait" or any command with arguments works.
  • For quick aliases, export it once in your shell profile.

docs.title: /edit: redo the last message
docs.text:
/edit reopens the last user message in the same editor and resends it: the edited text replaces the old message, everything after it is dropped and the model answers again. It is the undo/retry family's scalpel — /retry resends unchanged, /undo just drops.

Tested flow:

llama3.2:3b › Name one color. Answer with one word.
Blue
llama3.2:3b › /edit
resending edited message…
Apple

The editor was prefilled with the original message and returned Name one fruit. Answer with one word.; the old exchange was replaced, not appended. An empty result cancels (edit cancelled) and nothing is sent.

docs.title: Front ends
docs.text: The inline REPL binds Ctrl+G to the current input. In the deprecated Textual TUI the same key opens $EDITOR; /edit works in both.

docs.title: @file mentions
docs.text: @path in a prompt inlines the file's contents into the message: the model sees the text itself, not the path. It works in the REPL, in one-shot prompts and for piped stdin alike, and is the quick way to hand a file to a model without a tool call.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
• @ immediately before a path; the path runs to the next whitespace.
  • ~ expands to your home; relative paths resolve against the working directory the harness runs in.
  • Several mentions in one prompt are all inlined.
  • In the REPL, Tab completes @files along with commands, ids and model names.

The contents are appended to the message as one block per file, so the model can tell where a file starts and ends:

<file name="/tmp/notes.txt">
The fjord holds a copper coin of moon.
Second line, unremarkable.
</file>

The path is part of the block header; the user message itself keeps the mention as typed, and the session records the resolved paths so /show and exports can list what was sent.

docs.title: Tested examples
docs.text:
With this file:

$ printf 'The fjord holds a copper coin of moon.\nSecond line, unremarkable.\n' > /tmp/notes.txt

Ask about it — note the space before the ?, which is what ends the path:

$ ollamarun --no-tools --no-save llama3.2:3b "What is the first line of @/tmp/notes.txt ? Reply with just that line, verbatim."
llama3.2:3b ›
The fjord holds a copper coin of moon.

A missing file and an over-limit file both warn and are skipped (the model simply does not get them):

$ ollamarun --no-tools --no-save llama3.2:3b "Summarize @/tmp/nope.txt in one word."
@/tmp/nope.txt: no such file
llama3.2:3b ›
I don't see any file at `/tmp/nope.txt`.

$ ollamarun --no-tools --no-save llama3.2:3b "Summarize @/tmp/big.txt in one word."
@/tmp/big.txt: 300 KiB exceeds 256 KiB limit

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
Setting Default Meaning max_file_kb (config) 256 Files larger than this are skipped with a warning. — — Files are read as UTF-8 with undecodable bytes replaced.

Because the content is appended to the prompt, a big file eats the context window — the context counter and /context show the damage, and compaction can trim older messages.

Punctuation ends the mention

The path ends only at whitespace, so a sentence-final ./,/) right after the mention becomes part of the filename and the file is not inlined:

$ ollamarun --no-tools --no-save llama3.2:3b "Summarize @/tmp/notes.txt. One word."
@/tmp/notes.txt.: no such file

Put a space between the path and the punctuation (@/tmp/notes.txt .) or reorder the sentence. Tracked as issue #39.

docs.title: Where it fits
docs.text:
• Images and vision attaches images the same way, but as vision input instead of text.
  • The file tools (read_file, write_file, …) let the model decide what to touch; @file is you deciding up front.

docs.title: Images and vision
docs.text: Images ride along with a message as vision input. They are attached to the next message only — once it is sent, the attachment is spent, and /image clear throws pending ones away.

docs.title: Attaching
docs.text:
Way When --image PATH (repeatable) At launch, for a one-shot or the REPL's first message. /image PATH… In the REPL, for the next message. /image clear Drop everything pending.

The command answers with what it queued:

minicpm-v4.6:1b › /image /tmp/red.png
attached red.png
minicpm-v4.6:1b › What color fills the attached image? Answer with one word.
red

The model must advertise vision. Asking a text-only model makes the backend refuse the request, and the harness surfaces that as an ordinary error:

$ ollamarun --no-tools --no-save --image /tmp/red.png llama3.2:3b "What color is this image?"
llama3.2:3b ›
HTTP 400 on /api/chat: Multimodal data provided, but model does not support
multimodal requests.

A missing file exits 2 with the path as the message — currently without further context (tracked as issue #40):

$ ollamarun --no-save --image /tmp/does-not-exist.png llama3.2:3b "hi"
/tmp/does-not-exist.png
$ echo $?
2

docs.title: How they are sent
docs.text:
Images are base64-embedded into the chat request (images on the Ollama message), so nothing about the target machine matters: with --remote the file stays local and travels with the request.

  • Config image_storage (default "embed") keeps the bytes in the pending record. With any other value, files over 8 MiB are kept as a path and re-read when the request is built instead of being embedded twice.
  • Everything is read from disk at attach time, so editing the file afterwards does not change what was sent (in embed mode).

docs.title: The API side
docs.text: ollamarun serve takes images as OpenAI image_url parts (data URIs or http(s) URLs) or as uploaded file parts, with its own capability check and limits — see Vision and Artifacts.

docs.title: Pager
docs.text:
--pager (config pager: true) buffers the response and opens it in the system pager when it is complete, instead of streaming it into the scrollback:

$ PAGER=cat ollamarun --no-tools --pager llama3.2:3b "Reply with a two-item markdown bullet list of primary colors."
 • Red
 • Blue

The pager is the standard one: rich hands the content to pydoc's pager, which uses $PAGER (commonly less; PAGER=cat above prints it straight through, which is also what happens when the output is piped). Inside the pager you scroll and search the way that tool works; quitting it returns to the prompt.

/pager [on|off] toggles it mid-session:

llama3.2:3b › /pager on
pager: on

What lands in the pager is the finished answer with the same rendering — including the thinking panel when it is visible, and the response divider when a tool loop preceded it. What you lose is the live view: while the model generates, the terminal stays quiet and the footer does not tick. For long answers in a short terminal that trade is worth it; for watching progress it is not.

  • Streaming markdown — the live path.
  • Transcript replay — scrolling a session after the fact instead of during.

docs.title: Remote inference
docs.text: --remote NAME (config remote/remote_hosts) runs the whole thing on another machine: inference, model management (load/unload, /api/ps) and /pull happen there, while sessions, files, images and the tool harness stay local — there is no separate remote code path. Names resolve through tailscale status --json (falling back to the MagicDNS name), and any host[:port] works. Short names come from the config's remote_hosts map — the shipped entries are just my own fleet, so replace them with yours. A short /api/version preflight fails fast with the Tailscale node state when the machine is down, and resuming a session reconnects to the machine it last ran on.

docs.title: The REPL
docs.text: With no PROMPT argument, ollamarun starts the interactive front end: the inline prompt_toolkit REPL (the default, --ui inline). A model-less run opens the picker first.

docs.title: Starting up
docs.text:
$ ollamarun llama3.2:3b

The banner names what is in effect:

╭─ ollamarun ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ model   llama3.2:3b                                                  │
│ session 20261018-105614-b08e · new session                           │
│ host    http://127.0.0.1:11434                                       │
│ render  markdown · thinking collapsed · 95 local models              │
│ /help for commands · Ctrl+D to exit · Ctrl+T thinking                │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
llama3.2:3b ›

The model starts loading in the background the moment the session opens — the prompt is available immediately, with a waiting for <model>… spinner on its right while the load runs. When the model becomes resident, a one-time ollama ps table prints what is loaded and for how long.

docs.title: Typing prompts
docs.text:
• Plain text goes to the model and streams back with the live footer and, for thinking models, the collapsed thinking panel.
  • @path inlines a file's contents — see @file mentions.
  • /command runs a slash command — the full set is in Slash commands.
  • Tab completes commands, session ids, model names and @files.
  • Up/Down walks the prompt history (kept in ~/etc/data/ollamarun/history; set OLLAMA_NOHISTORY to disable it).
  • Ctrl+J inserts a newline for multi-line prompts.
  • Ctrl+R searches the prompt history.
  • Ctrl+G opens $OLLAMA_EDITOR on the current input — see Editor.
  • Ctrl+D leaves (equivalent to /bye).

docs.title: While an answer streams
docs.text:
The input line becomes a rule above the live view; keystrokes are not read until the turn ends. Two keys work mid-stream:

  • Ctrl+T expands the thinking panel in place; press it again to collapse. The stream never pauses either way.
  • Ctrl+C cancels: generation stops, providers that support abort are told to stop, and the prompt returns with a cancelled note.
llama3.2:3b › ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cancelled
llama3.2:3b ›

(The queueing behavior — typing ahead while the model works and having the message land at the next sub-task boundary — belongs to the deprecated Textual TUI; the inline REPL reads one line at a time.)

docs.title: Help inside the session
docs.text:
/help prints the command table; /help shortcuts the key bindings:

╭─────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ key     │ action                                                         │
├─────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Ctrl+D  │ exit                                                           │
│ Ctrl+C  │ cancel input / generation                                      │
│ Ctrl+T  │ expand or collapse the thinking panel while a response streams │
│ Ctrl+G  │ $OLLAMA_EDITOR for the current prompt                          │
│ Ctrl+J  │ insert newline                                                 │
│ Ctrl+R  │ search prompt history                                          │
│ Up/Down │ history navigation                                             │
│ Tab     │ complete commands, ids, models, @files                         │
│ @path   │ inline a file into the prompt                                  │
╰─────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

docs.title: Leaving
docs.text:
/bye (or /exit, or Ctrl+D) ends the session. The session is saved on the way out, and — unless --keep-loaded / config unload_on_exit: false — the model is unloaded:

llama3.2:3b › /bye
session 20261018-105614-b08e saved · ~/etc/data/ollamarun/sessions

Sessions are persistent: -c continues the most recent one and --session NAME continues a named one.

Without prompt_toolkit

prompt_toolkit powers the input line. If the package is missing (or the output is not a terminal), the REPL still runs, but with plain input() prompts: no Tab completion, no history, no Ctrl+G/Ctrl+R. Install it as shown in Installation to get the real thing.

docs.title: The other front end
docs.text: --ui tui starts the Textual TUI — panes, an always-available input box and a message queue. It is deprecated ahead of the web-UI rewrite; the inline REPL is the supported front end.

docs.title: Usage and flags
docs.text:
Every ollama run flag (ollama 0.34) is accepted, and the harness adds its own on top. Three invocation shapes:

$ ollamarun [flags] MODEL [PROMPT]      # flags first
$ ollamarun MODEL [PROMPT] [flags]      # or after the prompt
$ ollamarun                             # no model: picker, then the REPL

With a prompt the run is one generation and exits; without one it is the interactive REPL (a piped stdin counts as the prompt too).

Keep flags out of the middle

A flag between MODEL and PROMPT — ollamarun llama3.2:3b --no-tools "hi" — is an argument-parsing error (unrecognized arguments: hi). Put the flags before the model or after the prompt, as above. (Tracked as issue #37.)

The reference below is the same surface as ollamarun --help, grouped by what the flags are for.

docs.title: Model and server
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning MODEL (positional) — Model name; omit it to open the picker. -m MODEL, --model MODEL — Same as the positional, for scripts that build arguments up. --host HOST[:PORT] OLLAMA_HOST or the host config key, then 127.0.0.1:11434 The Ollama server to talk to. --remote NAME — Run on a tailnet machine (pi, kiddo, g3, optiplex7070/optiplex, guri, or any host[:port]). See Remote inference. --pull off Pull the model when it is missing without asking (free-disk line and per-layer progress). See Pulling models. --sort KEY modified Order for the model picker and lists: modified, name, size, parameters, context (aliases like recent/newest work). See Picker and sorting. --insecure off Skip TLS verification for an HTTPS host (the same escape hatch ollama has).

docs.title: Prompt input
docs.text:
Flag Default Meaning --system TEXT built-in default Replace the system prompt for this run. See Prompts. --system-file FILE — Read the replacement from a file. --no-system — Send no system prompt at all. --option KEY=VALUE — A model option (-o temperature=0.7); repeatable. --options-json JSON — Model options as one JSON object. --image PATH — Attach an image for a vision model; repeatable. See Images and vision.

@path mentions inside the prompt inline files — see @file mentions.

docs.title: Context and placement
docs.text:
Flag Default Meaning --num-ctx [N\|max-gpu] model/server default Set the context window, or ask for the largest one that stays fully on the GPU. Capped to the model's trained maximum with a warning. --max-cpu N — With --num-ctx: raise the window until the model's host RAM fills N% (1-100) of the available DRAM. --probe off With --num-ctx max-gpu/--max-cpu: verify by loading the model and reading the split back from /api/ps. --gpu-layers SPEC auto N layers, P% of them, +N/-N adjustments, all, cpu or auto.

All of this (and how the fits are computed) lives in Context and placement.

docs.title: Output and rendering
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning --render {auto,markdown,plain,raw} auto auto = markdown on a terminal, plain when piped (an explicit markdown degrades to plain off-terminal too). --no-math off Disable LaTeX → Unicode conversion. See 2D math. --show-thinking collapsed Start with the thinking panel expanded. --hidethinking — Hide the thinking output. --no-tps off Hide the live tok/s + context footer. --nowordwrap off Don't wrap long lines to the terminal width. --pager off Buffer the answer into $PAGER (rich's pager) instead of streaming it in place. See Pager. --raw — Write only the answer text to stdout (no panels, no stats). --json — With a chat run: print the final Ollama response as JSON (model, message with thinking, usage, timings). With --list/--search: JSON output. --verbose off Obsolete for a terminal (timings always show there); adds the ⏱ timings line to piped/redirected output.

docs.title: Tools and speech
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning --tools on (config tools) Offer the built-in tool definitions to the model. --no-tools — Disable the tool harness for this run. -y, --yes off Auto-approve tool runs (and --delete). Use with care — see Approvals and policy. --speak config tts_auto Read every final answer aloud through tts-remote (fire-and-forget). --no-speak — Never auto-speak for this run.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
Flag Default Meaning -c [SESSION_ID], --continue [SESSION_ID] — Continue the latest session, or the given one. -r, --resume — Browse saved sessions and pick one. --session NAME — Continue the session saved under NAME, or create it. --new — Force a fresh session even with -c/--session. --title TEXT — Title for a new session. --tag TAG — Tag for the session; repeatable. --auto-title config auto_title Ask the model for a title after the first turn. --no-save off Keep this run out of the session store entirely.

Sessions and their files are covered in Sessions.

docs.title: Session inspection
docs.text:
These all share one output convention — a rich table on a terminal, or --json / --csv / --markdown with --out FILE for scripts:

Flag Meaning --list List saved sessions. --search TEXT Search messages across saved sessions. --show SESSION_ID Replay a saved transcript the way it looked live. --export SESSION_ID Export a session. --export-format {md,json,html} Export format (default md). --delete SESSION_ID Move a session to the trash (trash-put; asks first unless -y). --reindex Rebuild the session index from the session files. --out FILE Write the inspection output to a file instead of stdout.

See Search and export.

docs.title: Runtime and housekeeping
docs.text: Flag Default Meaning --timeout SECONDS 600 Per-request timeout. --keepalive DURATION config keepalive How long Ollama keeps the model loaded (5m, 2h, …). --think [STR] config think Thinking mode: true/false or high/medium/low for supported models. --unload off Unload the model when the program ends (one-shot included). --keep-loaded — Never unload on exit (overrides config unload_on_exit). --ui MODE inline inline, tui (deprecated) or auto. See TUI. --config FILE ~/etc/config_files/ollamarun.json Use a different config file. --debug off Log to ~/etc/logs/ollamarun.log. --version — Print the version and exit.

docs.title: Ollama-compatible pass-through
docs.text:
Accepted for parity with ollama run and mapped onto the harness: --think, --keepalive, --hidethinking, --nowordwrap, --verbose (see above), plus:

Flag Meaning --dimensions int Truncate output embeddings to this dimension (embedding models). --truncate [bool] For embedding models: truncate inputs over the context window (default true; --truncate=false errors instead). --format string Response format — json, or an inline JSON schema (Ollama's format). With a format set, the tool harness steps aside. --insecure Skip TLS verification (HTTPS hosts).

docs.title: Environment
docs.text: Variable Meaning OLLAMA_HOST Server address when neither --host nor --remote is given. OLLAMA_EDITOR Editor for Ctrl+G and /edit (falls back to $EDITOR, then vi). See Editor. OLLAMA_NOHISTORY Do not keep the prompt input history.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code When 0 Success — including a declined delete (kept) and a one-shot whose answer arrived. 1 Runtime failures: unknown session, connection/HTTP errors, a run that could not complete. 2 Usage and configuration errors: bad arguments, an invalid serve_* key, an unusable --config. 130 The run was cancelled (Ctrl+C).

docs.title: Compaction
docs.text:
/summarize compacts older messages into a summary, dropping the originals from the context while keeping the session's recent turns. Config auto_compact does the same automatically when the context fills up.

/context shows window usage, and the context_status tool reports the budget, free space and a wrap-up note past 80%.

docs.title: GPU layers
docs.text:
--gpu-layers SPEC / /gpu-layers sets how many layers run on the GPU: N, P% of the model's layers (block_count from /api/show), +N/-N adjustments (baseline: the current value, else a full offload), all, cpu or auto. It is stored in the session, re-resolved per model, wins over /set parameter num_gpu, and unloads a resident model so the next request reloads with the new placement.

The API exposes the same field per session — see Context fits.

docs.title: max-cpu
docs.text:
--max-cpu N fills DRAM instead: it raises the context until the model's host RAM reaches N% (1-100) of the DRAM available to it — /proc/meminfo's MemAvailable on the Ollama machine (one ssh probe for --remote hosts) plus the RAM the loaded model already holds (/api/ps size - size_vram, back when it reloads), less a max_cpu_overhead_mb allowance. The same per-layer KV, sliding-window, recurrent-state and weight-split profile decides the placement: some layers may stay on the GPU unless gpu-layers is cpu; a pinned layer count is honoured and only the host side counts.

--probe solves the measured footprint line the same way and never chooses a context above the target — see Probes and calibration. Compatible probe/resident data calibrates future CPU estimates as well; automatic GPU placement is checked before a cached slope is applied.

From the REPL: /num-ctx --max-cpu N [--probe].

docs.title: max-gpu
docs.text:
--max-gpu picks the largest context that still keeps the model fully on the GPU. The model is profiled first: /api/show's GGUF metadata supplies the per-layer KV geometry (hybrid attention, sliding windows and their per-layer key/value dims, MLA's compressed latent, recurrent ssm.* state) and the parameter count, /api/tags supplies the on-disk size and quantization, and the two are cross-checked (params × bytes/param; the model row in the report names all of it). Free VRAM (nvidia-smi, locally or over one ssh probe for --remote machines) is then reduced by llama.cpp's fit margin (max_gpu_margin_mb, 1 GiB by default); the separate max_gpu_overhead_mb reserve defaults to 0 because the fit margin already covers the buffers llama.cpp projects. Resident models' VRAM is credited back (it returns when they reload at the new context), and a pinned gpu-layers is honoured: the output layer and the topmost blocks are counted as the offloaded share, and the non-block weights (token embeddings, output layer, vision projector) are estimated rather than split evenly.

--probe then verifies by loading candidates and reading each real GPU split back from /api/ps, solving the measured bytes-per-token line for the capacity, and leaves the model warm at the largest 100%-GPU context — see Probes and calibration.

From the REPL: /num-ctx --max-gpu [--probe].

docs.title: num-ctx
docs.text:
/num-ctx sizes the window:

  • N sets it (capped to the model's max with a warning).

CLI forms: --num-ctx N | max-gpu, plus --probe and --max-cpu N. The fitting forms live in max-gpu, max-cpu and probes.

docs.title: Context and placement
docs.text:
Two things decide how the model runs: the context window and its GPU placement.

  • /num-ctx sizes the window; max-gpu and max-cpu fit it to the machine, and probes verify by loading.
  • /gpu-layers pins how many layers run on the GPU.
  • /context reports window usage, and the footer's ctx counter ticks live — its denominator is the window the model is actually loaded with (/api/ps; a session num_ctx wins, the architectural maximum is only the fallback).
  • Compaction keeps long sessions inside the window.

The CLI takes the same as --num-ctx, --gpu-layers and --probe; the API exposes it per session — see Context fits.

docs.title: Probes and calibration
docs.text:
--probe turns an estimate into a measurement: candidates are actually loaded and each real GPU split is read back from /api/ps, solving the measured bytes-per-token line for the capacity. Both max-gpu and max-cpu take it (/num-ctx --max-gpu --probe, /num-ctx --max-cpu N --probe).

Resident and probe measurements calibrate future estimates using a conservative per-token slope and fixed overhead; the profile formula remains the fallback. The bounded cache is scoped to model digest, host, hardware, placement and KV settings, expires after 180 days, and is stored at ~/etc/data/ollamarun/ctxfit-calibration.json.

Config knobs: max_gpu_margin_mb (1 GiB), max_gpu_overhead_mb (0; the fit margin already covers llama.cpp's projected buffers), max_gpu_probes (10), max_cpu_overhead_mb (256 MiB) and max_cpu_probes (10).

docs.title: Embeddings
docs.text:
Embedding-capability models route to /api/embed honoring --dimensions/--truncate instead of chat.

The API surface exposes the same thing: POST /v1/embeddings, gated on the model's embedding capability. See Embeddings.

docs.title: Load, unload and residency
docs.text:
Unloading is deliberate, not left to the server:

  • /model and /load --model unload the current model before switching.
  • /load SESSION prompts current-vs-last model and unloads when switching.
  • REPL exit unloads (unload_on_exit config, --keep-loaded disables, --unload also unloads after one-shots).
  • Embedding models are never unloaded.

/ps shows the resident models (ollama ps).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Session parameters are Ollama options that ride every request:

  • /set parameter NAME VALUE sets one, /params shows them, and --option K=V seeds them at launch.
  • They live in the session, so they persist across resume, /save and the API's session records (settings.parameters).
  • num_gpu set here is overridden by a pinned gpu-layers value.

/show parameters shows the model's own parameters. System prompts are set separately — see Prompts.

docs.title: Picker and sorting
docs.text:
The model picker (a model-less ollamarun run, /model) sorts by modified (newest first), name, size, parameters or context; --sort KEY seeds it and the picker prompt takes --sort KEY in place. context costs one lazy /api/show per model, cached per host.

In the REPL, /model//models [NAME|--list|--sort KEY] switches model or lists and sorts the installed models, and /ps shows the resident ones.

docs.title: Pulling models
docs.text: A model missing from the target machine (local or --remote) offers to pull it after printing that machine's free disk space (local disk_usage, remote via a BatchMode ssh df probe; degrades to unknown), with live per-layer progress. --pull pulls without asking, /pull [MODEL] does it from the REPL, and declining the prompt opens the model picker.

docs.title: Live tok/s and context
docs.text:
~24.0 tok/s (avg 21.4) · 45 tok · ctx 12.345k/32.768k (38.123%)

The 5s windowed rate, its cumulative average, the streamed token count and a context counter that ticks with every token. Its denominator is the window the model is actually loaded with (/api/ps; a session num_ctx wins, the architectural maximum is only the fallback), and counts read raw below 1k / 3-decimal k above. The TUI status bar shows the same rate, average and live ctx. --no-tps//tps switch the footer off.

docs.title: Timings
docs.text: ⏱ load … · prompt … · eval … · total … prints under every answer on a terminal; --verbose is obsolete there and now only adds the line to piped/redirected output. --raw/--json never get it, and config show_stats: false turns it off.

docs.title: Streaming markdown
docs.text:
Output streams through a rich.Live view with a throttled markdown re-render (raw streaming past max_render_chars, default 12000); --pager buffers into the pager, --render markdown|plain|raw picks the mode.

  • 2D math — the display-math layout engine.
  • Thinking panel — the collapsible reasoning preview.
  • Footer — tok/s, the context counter and timings.
  • Transcript replay — saved sessions rendered the way they looked live.

docs.title: 2D math
docs.text: Display math ($$…$$, \[…\]) is laid out by a self-contained parser/layout engine — stacked fractions, sqrt overlines, sum/prod/lim limits above-below, integral side-limits, matrices, cases, aligned, \boxed, \binom, tall delimiters, accents, \mathbb/\mathcal/\mathfrak/\mathbf — centered in cyan, with flattened Unicode for inline math and pylatexenc as the never-crashing fallback (unknown env/over-wide/over-budget). --no-math / /math disable the conversion.

docs.title: Thinking panel
docs.text: Thinking streams live and is collapsed by default as an animated thinking · N chars · Ctrl+T to expand line. Ctrl+T expands a tail-capped boxed preview in place (press again to collapse; the stream never pauses), and /thinking full prints the stored panel later. --show-thinking/ --hidethinking and config thinking set the start mode.

docs.title: Transcript replay
docs.text: Calls and results are kept in the session, so --show ID replays the whole run the way it looked live — the same panels, colours and thinking. See Search and export for the session viewer and the shared output convention.

docs.title: Branching
docs.text:
/branch [TITLE] forks the conversation into a new session, leaving the current one untouched — the safe way to explore a different direction without losing the path you were on.

llama3.2:3b › /branch side quest
branched 20261018-122252-de60

The current session is saved first, then the branch is created as a full copy and becomes the active session. Everything conversational and behavioral comes along:

  • all messages so far (the branch starts with the same history),
  • system, parameters, think, keepalive, format, gpu_layers,
  • tags, stats, the approval tool_allow fingerprints and tool_rules,
  • tools_disabled and the tts settings.

What it does not copy: the title (unless you pass one, it becomes <original title> (branch)) and the id — the branch is an independent session from the moment it is created, so future turns on either side never interfere.

Typical uses:

  • Try an alternative. Branch, then /retry or /edit on the branch; the original stays exactly as it was.
  • Fork at a decision point. Get a file to a working state, branch, and keep one line of work "clean" while you experiment.
  • Split a long session into per-topic children before the context gets tight.

Going back is ordinary session work: /sessions (or -c/--session/ --show from the CLI) lists both, and the original is one pick away. The prompt column in /sessions shows the title, so (branch) children are easy to spot.

See Search and export for finding a parent again by content, and Save and load for resuming options.

docs.title: Save and load
docs.text: Every interactive session and every one-shot (unless --no-save) lands in the store, and any of them can be picked back up — from the command line or from inside the REPL.

docs.title: Resuming from the command line
docs.text:
Form Meaning -c [ID], --continue [ID] Continue the most recent session, or the given one. -r, --resume Browse saved sessions and pick one. --session NAME Continue the session named NAME, or create it. --new Force a fresh session even with -c/--session.

A named session keeps its name as its title, and later runs can omit the model — it comes from the session:

$ ollamarun --no-tools --session demo llama3.2:3b "Remember the number 41. Reply with OK only."
OK
$ ollamarun --no-tools --session demo "What number did I ask you to remember? Answer with the number only."
41

-c continues the most recently updated session, with its model:

$ ollamarun --no-tools -c "Now add one to that number. Answer with the number only."
42

-c and similar prompts

Because stored titles are derived from prompts, a prompt that matches an existing title can be mistaken for a session reference by -c and get swallowed (the run then reports no prompt). Reusing prompt wording is the trigger; --session or --continue ID avoids it. Tracked as issue #44.

-r opens the same browser as /sessions: a table where you type a number, an id, a filter to narrow, or q to quit.

Resuming also reconnects to the machine the session last ran on, unless --host/--remote override it — see Remote.

docs.title: /load and switching
docs.text:
• /load SESSION resumes a saved session; when its model differs from the current one the harness asks which model to run and unloads the current one before switching.
  • /load MODEL (or /model NAME) switches the model instead, unloading the previous resident unless it is an embedding model.

docs.title: Saving a model out of a session
docs.text:
/save NAME bakes the current conversation into an Ollama model, using the session as its messages and the effective system prompt as its SYSTEM — a snapshot you can ollamarun NAME later:

llama3.2:3b › /save olladocs-test:latest
creating olladocs-test:latest from llama3.2:3b…
  using existing layer sha256:dde5aa3fc5ff…
  creating new layer sha256:7b935f8b1107…
  writing manifest
  success
created olladocs-test:latest — `ollamarun olladocs-test:latest`

(Created model above was removed again with the API's /api/delete after the check.)

docs.title: Starting over
docs.text:
Command Effect /clear Empties the context; keeps settings, keeps the file's identity (context cleared), starts a new id so the old file stays. /new [TITLE] Saves the current session and starts a brand-new one (new session 20261018-122626-02cd). /branch Forks instead of starting over — see Branching.

Both are also reachable by just starting another run with --new or a different --session.

docs.title: Titles and tags
docs.text: Created automatically from the first prompt, settable with --title, --tag, /title and /tag, or asked from the model with --auto-title: see Titles and tags.

docs.title: Search and export
docs.text: Four inspection commands read the store without touching it, all sharing one output convention: a rich table on a terminal, or --json / --csv / --markdown with --out FILE for scripts.

docs.title: --search — inside the messages
docs.text:
$ ollamarun --search color
                                 search: color
╭───────────────┬───────────────┬───────────────┬───────────────┬──────────────╮
│ id            │ title         │ model         │ updated_at    │ match        │
├───────────────┼───────────────┼───────────────┼───────────────┼──────────────┤
│ 20261018-113… │ What color    │ minicpm-v4.6… │ 2026-10-18T1… │ What color   │
│               │ fills the     │               │               │ fills the    │
│               │ attached      │               │               │ attached     │
│               │ image? …      │               │               │ image? …     │
│ 20261018-113… │ Reply with a  │ llama3.2:3b   │ 2026-10-18T1… │ …wo-item     │
│               │ two-item …    │               │               │ markdown …   │
╰───────────────┴───────────────┴───────────────┴───────────────┴──────────────╯

Search covers what is in the session files — including thinking, tool calls and results — since it scans the stored JSON.

docs.title: --show — replay a transcript
docs.text:
$ ollamarun --show 20261018-113558-13ec
────────── Use write_file to write the text hello-from-the-model to /t… ──────────
id 20261018-113558-13ec · model llama3.2:3b · created 2026-10-18 11:35:58 ·
updated 2026-10-18 11:37:11 · 4 messages
        ╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── you ─╮
        │ Use write_file to write the text hello-from-the-model to             │
        │ /tmp/olladocs-demo.txt. Then confirm you did it.                     │
        ╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ tool · write_file ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ { "append": false, "content": "hello-from-the-model",                        │
│   "path": "/tmp/olladocs-demo.txt" }                                         │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
╭─ tool · write_file · ok ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ wrote 20 chars to /tmp/olladocs-demo.txt                                     │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
The written text is indeed "hello-from-the-model" and its length is 20 characters.
1 turns · 2937 prompt tok · 51 completion tok · 71s total

It is the live view's rendering again — boxes, tool panels, colours, thinking — plus a stats line. In the REPL, /show [topic] shows model details (info, license, modelfile, …, ollama-style); the transcript replay is the CLI's --show ID.

docs.title: --export — take a session away
docs.text:
--export ID writes the session out; --export-format md|json|html picks the shape (default md). The markdown export serializes the tool calls as JSON blocks:

# Use write_file to write the text hello-from-the-model to /t…

- **id:** `20261018-113558-13ec`
- **model:** `llama3.2:3b`
- **created:** 2026-10-18T11:35:58.014222-03:00
- **updated:** 2026-10-18T11:37:11.740373-03:00

## User

Use write_file to write the text hello-from-the-model to /tmp/olladocs-demo.txt.
Then confirm you did it.

## Assistant

```json
[{"id": "call_1ftvnkvz", "function": {"name": "write_file",
  "arguments": {"path": "/tmp/olladocs-demo.txt", "content": "hello-from-the-model"}}}]
```

The JSON export is the session file plus the derived presentation fields (title, display_title) — the machine-readable copy. The HTML one renders the same transcript the replay shows into a self-contained styled document (recorder.export_html), which is what --out session.html is for.

Two open issues with the printed forms

  • Printing a machine format to a narrow terminal can wrap long lines (rich printing), which breaks --json/--csv parsing; --out FILE is immune. Tracked as issue #42.
  • --export-format html currently prints the transcript to stdout before the document, even with --out; the file itself is correct. Tracked as issue #43.

docs.title: --reindex
docs.text: --reindex rebuilds index.json from the session files. It is the repair step when the index ever drifts (a manual file copy, a killed process) — sessions themselves are the source of truth.

docs.title: The convention
docs.text:
Flag Effect --json JSON array of records (list/search) or the API payload (chat runs). --csv CSV with the table's columns. --markdown The same table as a markdown pipe table. --out FILE Write the format to a file instead of stdout.

All four commands accept them; without a format flag you get the rich table.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Sessions are the durable half of the harness. One conversation is one JSON file plus a shared index — a store, not a cache, and nothing is deleted without going through the trash.

docs.title: Where things live
docs.text:
Path What ~/etc/data/ollamarun/sessions/<id>.json One session file per conversation. ~/etc/data/ollamarun/index.json The list view's index: id, title, model, host, timestamps, counts, tags. ~/etc/data/ollamarun/index.json.lock The flock file guarding index read-modify-write. ~/etc/data/ollamarun/history Prompt input history (unless OLLAMA_NOHISTORY). ~/etc/data/ollamarun/artifacts/ The serve artifact store (Artifacts). ~/etc/data/ollamarun/ctxfit-calibration.json Context-fit measurements (Probes and calibration).

Session ids look like 20261018-122556-a496 (timestamp plus a short random suffix). Anywhere an id is taken — --show, --export, -c, /load — a unique prefix or an unambiguous title reference works, so you rarely type the whole thing.

docs.title: The session file

Messages carry role, content and ts, plus whatever the turn produced — the same data --show and the exports read back:

Field On Meaning thinking assistant The reasoning text a thinking model produced. tool_calls assistant The call array the model asked for. tool_name tool Which tool produced this result. images user Attached images (path/name/sha1/size, base64 when embedded). files user @file mentions that were inlined. cancelled either The turn was interrupted here.

Settings live on the session too: system, parameters, think, keepalive, format, gpu_layers, tools_disabled, the approval tool_allow/tool_rules, and the tts fields — so /load restores the whole working context, not just the chat.

docs.title: Writes are atomic, and the index is locked
docs.text: Saving goes through a temp file named per writer plus os.replace, so an interrupted write can never leave a half session. The index read-modify-write runs under a shared RLock and an exclusive flock on index.json.lock: a CLI saving while ollamarun serve runs cannot lose entries, and --reindex rebuilds the index from the session files if it ever drifts.

docs.title: Deletes go to the trash
docs.text:
--delete ID (asks; -y skips) and the store's delete move the session file to the XDG trash via trash-put — never a raw unlink:

$ ollamarun --delete 20261018-111147-a9d6 -y
trashed 20261018-111147-a9d6

The file is recoverable from ~/.local/share/Trash/ (with a .trashinfo recording where it came from), and --list no longer shows it. In the REPL, /clear empties the context but keeps the session's settings and starts a new id under the same file; /new saves the current session and starts a fresh one.

docs.title: Not every run is saved
docs.text:
--no-save keeps a run out of the store entirely — useful for scripting and for throwaway checks — and --json/--raw runs still respect it. The REPL's prompt history is the only other thing persisted by default, and OLLAMA_NOHISTORY disables that too.

  • Save and load — resuming conversations.
  • Search and export — getting data back out.

docs.title: Titles and tags
docs.text: Every session gets a title and can carry tags; both show up in the /sessions picker and --list, and both survive in the index.

docs.title: Titles
docs.text:
A new session is titled from its first prompt (naive_title() — the first line, trimmed to a sane length). --title TEXT sets one up front, and --auto-title asks the model for a better one via the title prompt:

$ ollamarun --no-tools --auto-title llama3.2:3b "Explain in one sentence what a haiku is."
llama3.2:3b ›
A haiku is a traditional Japanese poetry form consisting of three lines with
a syllable count of 5-7-5, often capturing a moment or image from nature.
$ ollamarun --list
| 20261018-122724-96a7 | Understanding Haiku Poetry Basics | llama3.2:3b | …

In the REPL:

Command Effect /title Show the current title. /title TEXT Set it. /title --auto Ask the model to (re)title from the first message.

The title is also the header of a transcript replay and the first column everywhere sessions are listed. Renaming is cheap — the title lives on the session, not in the filename.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Tags are a free-form list on the session. Set them at launch (--tag is repeatable) or in the REPL:

llama3.2:3b › /tag add demo docs
tags demo, docs
llama3.2:3b › /tag list
tags: demo, docs
llama3.2:3b › /tag rm docs
tags demo

/tag with no argument lists them; add/rm take several at once. Tags appear in --list/--search output and in the exported JSON, which makes them the light-weight way to group work (one tag per project, per machine, per experiment).

docs.title: Names, titles and ids
docs.text:
Three related things, easy to mix up:

  • id — 20261018-122556-a496, system-generated; any unique prefix works as a reference.
  • name — what --session NAME keys on; it is also stored as the title when the session is created that way.
  • title — the display label, derived from the prompt or set by --title//title/--auto-title.

--list shows the title; --show, --export and -c accept ids, id prefixes, names and title references.

docs.title: Undo, retry and edit
docs.text: Three ways to redo the recent past. All of them operate on the last exchange, where an exchange is everything from one user message through the model's answer — tool rounds included, so a turn that called tools goes away as one unit.

docs.title: /undo — drop the last exchange
docs.text:
llama3.2:3b › /undo
undone

The last user message and everything after it are removed, the stats' turn count drops by one, and the session is saved. With an empty history it says nothing to undo.

docs.title: /retry — ask again
docs.text:
llama3.2:3b › /retry
retrying…
llama3.2:3b › Blue

The last user message stays; every assistant/tool message after it is discarded and the request is made again, so you get a fresh sample. Retrying after a cancelled or failed answer is the usual reason.

docs.title: /edit — fix the question
docs.text:
/edit reopens the last user message in $OLLAMA_EDITOR, replaces it with what you save, drops the old answer and regenerates — the scalpel of the three:

llama3.2:3b › Name one color. Answer with one word.
Blue
llama3.2:3b › /edit
resending edited message…
Apple

The editor was prefilled with the original message and returned Name one fruit. Answer with one word.; the exchange was replaced, not appended. An empty editor result cancels (edit cancelled). Full mechanics on the Editor page.

docs.title: Which one?
docs.text:
Goal Command Forget the last exchange and go on /undo Same question, another answer /retry Change the question itself /edit Fork instead of rewriting /branch

All three keep the rest of the conversation (and every setting) intact, and all three are saved immediately — closing the session afterwards does not bring the undone exchange back.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
With tools on — the default — every chat request carries the built-in tool definitions, and the model can call them through Ollama function calling. The harness is the difference between a chat that says it listed your files and one that actually did: calls are executed locally behind an approval gate, their results go back to the model as tool messages, and the loop repeats until the model answers without asking for anything else.

  • The tool loop — what happens between a call and the answer.
  • Approvals and policy — the gate and its modes.
  • Definitions — the JSON the model sees, and how to change it.
  • Reference — every tool with its parameters.

docs.title: What the model gets
docs.text:
The request carries one schema per enabled tool, built from the definition files: name, description and JSON-schema parameters. Which tools are offered depends on the host:

Condition Tools Always run_shell, run_python, read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_dir, make_dir, move_file, copy_file, delete_file, fetch_url, search_sessions, list_models, system_status, context_status, session_info The ddgs package resolves web_search A tts-remote CLI resolves speak, list_voices A chemInventoryAPI CLI resolves (config chem_tools: true) chem_search, chem_container, chem_locations ollamarun serve runs an artifact store publish_artifact

Each tool also has aliases for names models tend to invent — /tools search off disables web_search, and a call to curl or mkdir resolves onto the real tool before the registry is searched. /tools NAME help lists a tool's aliases.

docs.title: The four ways a call is handled
docs.text:
1. Auto — read-only tools (read_file, list_dir, …) and the speak tool never ask.
  2. Safe list — allowlisted shell commands (ls, cat, grep, rg, read-only git, …) and provably harmless Python run unattended.
  3. Rules and remembered calls — a generalized rule or an exact remembered call from this session runs without asking.
  4. Ask — everything else asks in the REPL; in an unattended run it is denied with a note, unless -y/--yes or /tools policy auto is in effect.

Details and the prompt itself: Approvals and policy.

docs.text:
/tools is the dashboard — state, approval class and the policy line:

│ form                         │ what it does                                         │

│ help [NAME]                  │ this reference, or one tool's page                   │
